bg.1.28.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
roles: Shows the people he must oppose are his own.
bg.1.28.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

bg.1.29.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
roles: Trembling and hair standing on end.
bg.1.29.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥

bg.1.47.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
roles: Shows his mind overwhelmed by grief.
bg.1.47.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥

bg.10.1.m: Listen once more, mighty-armed, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your good, because you delight in it and are dear to me.
roles: Gives the teaching out of love.
bg.10.1.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥

bg.10.11.m: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
roles: Shows the clearing is his doing, out of compassion.

bg.10.20.m: I am the self, Gudakesha, seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.
roles: Shows the Lord is the inmost self of every being.
bg.10.20.sa: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥

bg.10.41.m: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that it springs from a spark of my splendour.
roles: Excellence anywhere becomes a reason for reverence.
bg.10.41.sa: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥

bg.10.9.m: With minds fixed on me and lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and delighted.
bg.10.9.sa: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥

bg.11.24.m: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colours, mouths wide open, with huge fiery eyes, my inner self trembles, Vishnu, and I find neither courage nor peace.
bg.11.24.sa: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णंव्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्माधृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥

scene.s: Arjuna sees all beings, gods and worlds in Krishna, and warriors rushing into his mouths like moths into flame. Terrified, he asks who Krishna really is.
scene.t: Arjuna sees the cosmic form and praises it

bg.11.33.m: Therefore stand up and win glory; conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; be merely the instrument, ambidextrous archer.
roles: Acting as an instrument of a will larger than one's own.
bg.11.33.sa: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्वजित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् । मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेवनिमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥

scene.s: Krishna declares he is Time, the destroyer of worlds; the warriors will die even without Arjuna, so he should rise and be the instrument.
scene.t: "I am Time": Krishna urges Arjuna to fight

bg.11.41.m: Whatever I said rashly, thinking of you as a friend, 'O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend', not knowing your greatness, out of carelessness or affection, and whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while at play, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in company, I ask your forgiveness for it, immeasurable one.
roles: Cultivates asking forgiveness without excuses for forgiveness.
bg.11.41.sa: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥

scene.s: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
scene.t: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form

bg.11.42.m: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while playing, resting, sitting or eating, alone or in front of others, Achyuta, I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable.
roles: Shows asking forgiveness plainly with nothing held back.

scene.s: Having seen Krishna's greatness, Arjuna remembers years of casual friendship.

bg.11.44.m: So, bowing and prostrating my body, I ask your grace, adorable Lord. As a father with his son, a friend with his friend, a lover with the beloved, please bear with me.
roles: Shows forgiveness asked for with the body bowed and no excuse.
bg.11.44.sa: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायंप्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् । पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युःप्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥

scene.s: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
scene.t: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form

bg.11.45.m: I am thrilled to have seen what was never seen before, yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me only that form of yours, God; be gracious, Lord of gods, refuge of the world.
roles: My mind is shaken with fear even while thrilled.
bg.11.45.sa: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वाभयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे । तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपंप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥

scene.s: Trembling, Arjuna praises Krishna, asks pardon for having treated him as just a friend, begs him to bear with him as a father, friend or lover would, and asks to see his familiar form.
scene.t: Terrified, Arjuna prays to see the gentle four-armed form

bg.11.49.m: Do not be afraid or bewildered at seeing this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and glad at heart, see again that same familiar form of mine.
roles: Shows being free from fear and glad at heart.
bg.11.49.sa: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावोदृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् । व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वंतदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥

scene.s: Krishna tells Arjuna not to fear, and returns to his familiar form to reassure him.
scene.t: Krishna returns to his gentle form

bg.11.50.m: Having spoken so, Vasudeva showed Arjuna his own form once more; the great-souled one, becoming gentle in form again, comforted the frightened Arjuna.
roles: Shows comfort given to the frightened one.
bg.11.50.sa: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वास्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः । आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनंभूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥

scene.s: Terrified by the cosmic vision, Arjuna begs to see his friend again; Krishna returns to his familiar form.

bg.11.51.m: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, Janardana, I have now come to myself; my mind is steady and I am back to my natural state.
roles: Depicts relief after terror returning to nature.
bg.11.51.sa: अर्जुन उवाचदृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन । इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥

scene.s: Arjuna sees Krishna's human face again after the overwhelming vision.

bg.11.54.m: But by undivided devotion, Arjuna, I can be known like this, seen in truth, and entered into, scorcher of foes.
roles: Shows devotion that looks to nothing else.
bg.11.54.sa: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥

bg.11.55.m: One who works for me, holds me as the highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity towards any being, comes to me, Pandava.
roles: Shows without enmity toward any being.
bg.11.55.sa: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः । निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥

bg.12.10.m: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on doing work for my sake. Even by doing actions for me, you will reach perfection.
bg.12.10.sa: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥

bg.12.11.m: If you cannot do even this, then taking refuge in my yoga and with self restrained, give up the fruit of all actions.
roles: Done while taking refuge in him.
bg.12.11.sa: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥

bg.12.12.m: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
roles: Shows peace follows immediately on giving up the fruit.

bg.12.13.m: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
roles: Compassion is named as a mark of the one dear to God shows compassion.
bg.12.13.sa: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥

bg.12.14.m: ever content, steady in practice, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding given to me, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
roles: Shows resolve as he is firm in resolve.
bg.12.14.sa: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥

bg.12.15.m: One from whom the world does not shrink and who does not shrink from the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and agitation, is dear to me.
roles: Names freedom from fear and agitation as a mark.
bg.12.15.sa: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥

bg.12.16.m: One who expects nothing, is pure, capable, unconcerned and untroubled, who has given up all self-centred undertakings, that devotee of mine is dear to me.
bg.12.16.sa: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥

bg.12.17.m: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of both good and bad, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.
roles: Gives no swing between elation and aversion.
bg.12.17.sa: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥

bg.12.18.m: One who is the same to enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, and free from attachment,
roles: Shows the same toward friend and foe, honour and insult.
bg.12.18.sa: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥

bg.12.19.m: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.
roles: Shows blame and praise weighing the same.
bg.12.19.sa: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥

bg.12.2.m: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, ever united, with supreme faith, I consider the most united with me.
roles: Shows the mind resting in him always.
bg.12.2.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥

bg.12.4.m: Restraining all the senses, even-minded everywhere, rejoicing in the welfare of all beings, they too reach me.
bg.12.4.sa: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥

bg.12.6.m: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.
bg.12.6.sa: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥

bg.12.7.m: For those whose minds are absorbed in me, O Partha, I very soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and endless change.
bg.12.7.sa: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥

bg.12.8.m: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding settle in me; from then on you will dwell in me. Of this there is no doubt.
roles: Shows mind and understanding placed in him.
bg.12.8.sa: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥

bg.12.9.m: If you cannot fix your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me by the yoga of practice, Dhananjaya.
roles: Shows the mind returning again and again.
bg.12.9.sa: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥

bg.13.25.m: Some see the self in the self by the self through meditation; others by the path of knowledge; and others by the yoga of action.
roles: Shows finding the way that fits.
bg.13.25.sa: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥

bg.13.26.m: Others, not knowing this, worship having heard it from others; they too cross beyond death, devoted to what they have heard.
roles: Cultivates devotion to what one has heard from teachers is enough to cross.
bg.13.26.sa: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥

bg.13.28.m: One who sees the Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the undying within the dying, truly sees.
roles: Seeing the one imperishable presence in all beings.
bg.13.28.sa: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥

bg.13.29.m: Seeing the Lord equally present everywhere, one does not injure the self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
roles: Shows the same Lord seen everywhere including in oneself.
bg.13.29.sa: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥

bg.13.33.m: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
bg.13.33.sa: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥

bg.13.8.m: Humility, freedom from pretence, non-violence, patience, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control,
roles: Shows forbearance is named among the means to knowledge.

bg.13.9.m: detachment from sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing clearly the pain and flaw in birth, death, old age and sickness,
roles: Repeatedly seeing pain built into birth, ageing, illness and death loosens the grip of pleasure.

bg.14.12.m: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
roles: Shows learning to read one's own state by its signs.
bg.14.12.sa: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥

bg.14.13.m: Darkness, inertia, heedlessness and delusion: these arise when tamas increases, joy of the Kurus.
roles: Shows reading one's state by its signs.
bg.14.13.sa: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥

bg.14.22.m: The Blessed Lord said: One who does not hate clarity, activity or delusion when they arise, Pandava, nor longs for them when they cease,
roles: Shows neither hating a state while it is here nor longing for it when it leaves.
bg.14.22.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥

bg.14.23.m: who sits like one unconcerned, unshaken by the qualities, who knows 'it is only the qualities moving' and stays firm without wavering,
roles: You are the one who watches the qualities move.
bg.14.23.sa: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥

bg.14.24.m: who is the same in pain and pleasure, at home in the self, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are alike, who is the same to the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, the same in blame and praise,
roles: Gives svastha resting in one's own self.

bg.14.25.m: the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, who has given up all self-driven undertakings: such a person is said to have gone beyond the qualities.
roles: Names honour and dishonour, friend and foe held alike.
bg.14.25.sa: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥

bg.14.8.m: Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep, Bharata.
roles: Shows knowing what is holding one down.
bg.14.8.sa: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥

bg.15.15.m: I am seated in the hearts of all. From me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am what is to be known by all the Vedas; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
roles: Gives memory and understanding as gifts.
bg.15.15.sa: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥

bg.15.5.m: Free from pride and delusion, with the fault of attachment conquered, ever dwelling in the self, desires turned away, freed from the pairs called pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that eternal state.
roles: Shows always dwelling on the self.
bg.15.5.sa: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥

bg.15.7.m: An eternal part of me becomes the living soul in the world of the living, and draws to itself the mind and the five senses that rest in nature.
roles: Shows the living self is an eternal part of the Lord.
bg.15.7.sa: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥

bg.16.1.m: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study, austerity and uprightness,
roles: Names fearlessness heading the list of divine qualities.
bg.16.1.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥

bg.16.11.m: Clinging to immeasurable worries that end only at death, taking the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, convinced that this is all,
roles: Gives endless worry to the belief that getting and enjoying is all there is.
bg.16.11.sa: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः ॥

scene.s: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
scene.t: The demonic nature and its downfall

bg.16.12.m: bound by hundreds of ties of hope, given over to desire and anger, they strive to amass wealth by unjust means for the enjoyment of desires.

scene.s: Krishna portrays people driven by endless desire and worry, bound by hundreds of hopes, always counting 'this I have, that I'll get', proud of wealth and birth.
scene.t: The demonic nature and its downfall

bg.16.13.m: 'This I have gained today; this desire I shall fulfil. This wealth is mine, and this too shall be mine.'
roles: Depicts the inner voice of never enough, quoted word for word.
bg.16.13.sa: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥

bg.16.15.m: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice': so they say, deluded by ignorance.
roles: Names 'who else is equal to me?'
bg.16.15.sa: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥

bg.16.17.m: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against the rules.
roles: Names giving or worship done for display is empty.
bg.16.17.sa: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥

bg.16.2.m: non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, peace, absence of slander, compassion for beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness,
roles: Shows compassion toward beings is named.
bg.16.2.sa: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥

bg.16.21.m: Threefold is the gate of hell that destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. Therefore one should give up these three.
roles: Names the three impulses to watch before they ruin a person.
bg.16.21.sa: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥

bg.16.22.m: Released from these three gates of darkness, Kaunteya, a person does what is good for the self and so reaches the highest goal.
roles: Shows acting for one's real good once the three are set down.
bg.16.22.sa: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥

bg.16.3.m: vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from excessive pride: these belong to one born with the divine nature, Bharata.
roles: Shows fortitude lifting body and senses when they flag.
bg.16.3.sa: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥

bg.16.4.m: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born with the demonic nature, Partha.
roles: Names the traits that take a person downward.
bg.16.4.sa: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥

bg.16.5.m: The divine nature leads to freedom, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava; you are born with the divine nature.
roles: Trusts in one's own good nature.
bg.16.5.sa: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥

bg.17.15.m: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
roles: Shows words chosen true, kind and helpful build goodwill.
bg.17.15.sa: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥

bg.17.16.m: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling: this is called austerity of the mind.
roles: Shows gentleness and clean intent toward others.

bg.17.18.m: Austerity practised to gain respect, honour and reverence, and with show, is called rajasic; it is unstable and fleeting.
roles: Asks whom the effort is for.
bg.17.18.sa: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् । क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥

bg.17.19.m: Austerity performed out of foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to harm another, is called tamasic.
roles: Gives toward oneself, torment is not required.
bg.17.19.sa: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः । परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥

bg.17.20.m: A gift given because it is right to give, to one who does nothing in return, at the right place and time and to a worthy person, is called sattvic.
roles: Shows giving because it is right to give.
bg.17.20.sa: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥

bg.17.21.m: But a gift given in expectation of a return, or with a view to reward, or given reluctantly, is called rajasic.
roles: Names a test of one's own motive in giving.
bg.17.21.sa: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥

bg.17.3.m: Everyone's faith follows their nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith; as a person's faith is, so is that person.
roles: Treats faith as the stuff a person is made of.
bg.17.3.sa: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥

bg.17.8.m: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are flavourful, soothing, nourishing and agreeable, are dear to the sattvic.
roles: Shows food chosen for clarity and cheer.
bg.17.8.sa: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥

bg.18.10.m: The wise renouncer, full of clarity and free of doubt, does not hate disagreeable work nor cling to agreeable work.
roles: Shows the same toward pleasant and unpleasant duty.
bg.18.10.sa: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते । त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥

bg.18.11.m: It is not possible for an embodied being to give up action entirely. But one who gives up the fruit of action is called a renouncer.
roles: Shows renunciation relocated from the work to its fruit.
bg.18.11.sa: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः । यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥

bg.18.14.m: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence: these are the five causes of every action.
roles: Names credit and blame as both shared.
bg.18.14.sa: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥

bg.18.16.m: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
roles: The pure self is not the doer.
bg.18.16.sa: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥

bg.18.20.m: The knowledge by which one sees one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided, know that knowledge to be sattvic.
roles: Shows one imperishable reality in every being.
bg.18.20.sa: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥

bg.18.23.m: Action that is obligatory, done without attachment, without love or hatred, by one who does not crave its fruit, is called sattvic.
roles: Not driven by like or dislike.
bg.18.23.sa: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥

bg.18.24.m: But action done by one seeking desires, or with ego, or with great strain, is called rajasic.
roles: Shows asking what is driving the effort.
bg.18.24.sa: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥

bg.18.25.m: Action undertaken out of delusion, without regard to consequence, loss, injury to others, or one's own ability, is called tamasic.
roles: Shows weighing what follows, what it costs, whom it hurts, and what one can carry before acting.
bg.18.25.sa: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥

bg.18.26.m: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
roles: Names steadiness as what the best doer carries.
bg.18.26.sa: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥

bg.18.27.m: The doer who is passionate, eager for the fruits of work, greedy, harmful, impure, and swayed by joy and sorrow, is called rajasic.
roles: Names being tossed by joy and grief over results.
bg.18.27.sa: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥

bg.18.28.m: The doer who is undisciplined, vulgar, obstinate, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent and procrastinating, is called tamasic.
bg.18.28.sa: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥

bg.18.30.m: The understanding that knows action and withdrawal, what should and should not be done, what is to be feared and what not, bondage and freedom, that understanding is sattvic, Partha.
roles: Shows discernment of what should and should not be done.
bg.18.30.sa: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥

bg.18.31.m: The understanding by which one wrongly knows right and wrong, what should and should not be done, that understanding, Partha, is rajasic.
roles: Shows a restless mind misjudges right and wrong; settle it before deciding.
bg.18.31.sa: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च । अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥

bg.18.32.m: The understanding which, wrapped in darkness, thinks wrong is right and sees all things in reverse, Partha, is tamasic.
roles: Names the possibility that one's certainty is upside down.
bg.18.32.sa: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता । सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥

bg.18.33.m: The firmness by which one holds the workings of the mind, breath and senses through unwavering yoga, that firmness, Partha, is sattvic.
roles: Shows steadiness defined as holding mind, breath and senses on course.
bg.18.33.sa: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः । योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥

bg.18.34.m: But the firmness by which one holds to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, craving their fruits, Arjuna, that firmness, Partha, is rajasic.
roles: Shows asking what one's determination is in service of.
bg.18.34.sa: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन । प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥

bg.18.35.m: The firmness by which a dull-minded person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and pride, that firmness, Partha, is tamasic.
bg.18.35.sa: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च । न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥

bg.18.36.m: Now hear from me the three kinds of happiness, best of the Bharatas: the happiness one comes to enjoy through practice, and in which one reaches the end of sorrow.
roles: Shows delight that comes through practice.
bg.18.36.sa: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥

bg.18.37.m: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from the clarity of one's own understanding, is called sattvic happiness.
roles: Gives a reason to stay through the hard beginning.
bg.18.37.sa: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥

bg.18.38.m: The happiness that comes from contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called rajasic.
roles: Shows a test for telling two kinds of happiness apart by how they end.
bg.18.38.sa: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥

bg.18.39.m: The happiness that deludes the self in the beginning and in the end, arising from sleep, laziness and heedlessness, is called tamasic.
roles: Shows happiness tested by whether it dulls.
bg.18.39.sa: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥

bg.18.45.m: Each person, devoted to his own work, attains perfection. Hear how one devoted to his own work finds perfection.
bg.18.45.sa: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥

bg.18.46.m: By worshipping, through his own work, Him from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
roles: Shows one's own work as worship.
bg.18.46.sa: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥

bg.18.47.m: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
roles: Self-respect in doing one's own work, flaws included.
bg.18.47.sa: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥

bg.18.48.m: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
roles: Shows staying with one's work through its faults.
bg.18.48.sa: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥

bg.18.49.m: One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered himself and is free from desire, reaches through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.
roles: Shows actionlessness abiding as the actionless self.
bg.18.49.sa: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥

bg.18.53.m: Having given up ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free from the sense of 'mine' and peaceful, one becomes fit to be one with Brahman.
bg.18.53.sa: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥

bg.18.54.m: Become one with Brahman, serene in self, one neither grieves nor craves. The same to all beings, one gains supreme devotion to me.
roles: Shows the serene self of one established in Brahman.
bg.18.54.sa: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥

bg.18.56.m: Even while always doing every kind of work, the one who leans on me reaches the eternal, imperishable home by my grace.
roles: Shows leaning on him while working.
bg.18.56.sa: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥

bg.18.57.m: Mentally resigning all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
roles: Shows all actions resigned to him in the mind.
bg.18.57.sa: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥

bg.18.58.m: Fixing your mind on me, you will cross over all obstacles by my grace. But if out of ego you will not listen, you will perish.
roles: Shows keeping the mind on him.
bg.18.58.sa: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि । अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥

scene.s: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.

bg.18.6.m: But even these actions should be done giving up attachment and fruits. This, Partha, is my definite and highest view.
roles: No clinging even to one's good deeds.
bg.18.6.sa: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च । कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम् ॥

bg.18.61.m: The Lord dwells in the heart of every being, Arjuna, moving all beings by his power as if mounted on a machine.
roles: Shows taking refuge in him alone.
bg.18.61.sa: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥

bg.18.62.m: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
roles: Gives supreme peace promised through grace.
bg.18.62.sa: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥

bg.18.63.m: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
roles: Names the choice after reflection as one's own.
bg.18.63.sa: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥

scene.s: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.

bg.18.64.m: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.
bg.18.64.sa: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥

bg.18.65.m: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
roles: Shows mind, love, worship and bowing all turned to him.
bg.18.65.sa: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥

bg.18.66.m: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.
roles: Shows the promise removes the fear of what one's wrongs will cost.
bg.18.66.sa: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥

scene.s: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.

bg.18.7.m: Renunciation of obligatory action is not proper. Its abandonment out of delusion is declared tamasic.
roles: Asks whether walking away comes from clear sight or confusion.
bg.18.7.sa: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते । मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥

bg.18.73.m: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed and I have regained my memory through your grace, Achyuta. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.
roles: Shows resolve sounding like this after real doubt.
bg.18.73.sa: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत । स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥

scene.s: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.

bg.18.78.m: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the archer, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and sound policy. This is my conviction.
roles: Shows victory and wellbeing are assured there.
bg.18.78.sa: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥

bg.18.8.m: One who gives up work because it is painful, out of fear of bodily strain, performs rajasic renunciation and does not gain its fruit.
roles: Shows staying with a duty through discomfort.
bg.18.8.sa: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥

bg.18.9.m: When necessary work is done simply because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and the fruit, that renunciation is considered sattvic.
roles: Shows doing what must be done because it must be done.
bg.18.9.sa: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन । सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥

bg.2.11.m: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.
roles: Names the confusion of grieving while arguing wisely, and opens the teaching on what does not die.
bg.2.11.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥

scene.s: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
scene.t: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)

bg.2.12.m: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; nor will there ever be a time when all of us cease to be.
roles: Names the self present in all three times.
bg.2.12.sa: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥

bg.2.13.m: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this.
roles: Points to the one who remains while the body's stages pass.
bg.2.13.sa: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥

bg.2.14.m: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
roles: Bearing what passes without being moved.

bg.2.15.m: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for immortality.
roles: The steady person is not thrown by what passes.
bg.2.15.sa: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥

bg.2.16.m: The unreal has no lasting being, and the real never ceases to be. Those who see the truth have seen the final word on both.
roles: Shows the real as that which never ceases.
bg.2.16.sa: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥

bg.2.20.m: It is never born and never dies; having been, it will not cease to be. Unborn, eternal, constant and ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.
roles: Shows nothing that can happen to the body reaches it.
bg.2.20.sa: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥

bg.2.22.m: Just as a person casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the embodied self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.
roles: The wearer is other than what is worn.
bg.2.22.sa: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहायनवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥

bg.2.23.m: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.
roles: Nothing can cut, burn, drown or wither it.
bg.2.23.sa: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥

bg.2.25.m: It is called unmanifest, unthinkable and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.
roles: Gives the self as beyond the senses, beyond thought, beyond change.

bg.2.26.m: And even if you think of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, still, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve like this.
roles: Cultivates reasoning from one's own view of birth and death.
bg.2.26.sa: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥

bg.2.27.m: Death is certain for the one who is born, and birth is certain for the one who dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
roles: Shows steadiness before what cannot be changed.
bg.2.27.sa: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥

bg.2.28.m: Beings are unseen in their beginning, seen in their middle, and unseen again in their end, Arjuna. What is there to lament in this?
roles: Shows a life as an appearing between two unseen states.
bg.2.28.sa: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥

bg.2.30.m: The self dwelling in the body of every being is eternal and can never be slain, Bharata. Therefore you should not grieve for any creature.
roles: Names the deathless indweller of every body.
bg.2.30.sa: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥

bg.2.38.m: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, then engage in the fight. Done this way, you will incur no wrong.
roles: Shows gain and loss, win and defeat held alike.
bg.2.38.sa: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥

bg.2.40.m: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
roles: Shows supporting the decision to start small.
bg.2.40.sa: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥

bg.2.41.m: Here, Arjuna, the resolute mind is one-pointed. But the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
bg.2.41.sa: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥

bg.2.44.m: For those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, a resolute, settled understanding does not arise.
bg.2.44.sa: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥

bg.2.45.m: The Vedas deal with the three qualities; rise above them, Arjuna. Be free from the pairs of opposites, always steady in goodness, free from the urge to acquire and keep, and possessed of the self.
roles: Shows being possessed of the self.
bg.2.45.sa: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥

bg.2.47.m: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
roles: Shows work done without the fruit as motive staying even.
bg.2.47.sa: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥

bg.2.48.m: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
roles: Gives evenness as the very definition of yoga.
bg.2.48.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥

bg.2.49.m: Action done for its rewards is far inferior to action done with a steady mind. Seek refuge in that understanding; those who work only for the fruit are to be pitied.
bg.2.49.sa: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥

bg.2.50.m: One joined to this understanding casts off both good and bad results here. So devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.
roles: Shows evenness of mind in work.
bg.2.50.sa: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥

bg.2.52.m: When your understanding crosses the mire of delusion, you will grow indifferent to all that you have heard and all that is yet to be heard.
bg.2.52.sa: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥

bg.2.53.m: When your understanding, now confused by conflicting things you have heard, stands firm and unmoving in deep stillness, then you will attain yoga.
roles: Cultivates an understanding that stands unmoving.
bg.2.53.sa: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥

bg.2.55.m: The Blessed Lord said: When a person gives up all the desires of the mind and is content in the self by the self, then he is called one of steady wisdom.
roles: Shows the self is itself the source of satisfaction.
bg.2.55.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥

bg.2.56.m: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who has no craving for pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.

bg.2.57.m: One who is without attachment anywhere, who neither rejoices on meeting good nor hates on meeting bad, has wisdom that is firmly set.
roles: Shows no elation at the good, no bitterness at the bad.
bg.2.57.sa: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥

bg.2.58.m: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs on every side, a person withdraws the senses from their objects, his wisdom is firmly set.
roles: Shows wisdom staying set when the senses are gathered.
bg.2.58.sa: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥

bg.2.59.m: Objects fall away from one who abstains from them, but the taste for them remains. Even the taste falls away once the Supreme is seen.
roles: Shows the taste goes when the highest is seen.
bg.2.59.sa: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥

bg.2.6.m: Nor do we know which is better for us, to fight or not, or whether we will win or they will. The very people after whose death we would not wish to live stand facing us.
roles: Shows either outcome as a loss where neither is better.
bg.2.6.sa: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥

bg.2.60.m: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind even of a wise person who is striving, Arjuna.
roles: Names the pull of the senses as strong so a slip is no surprise.
bg.2.60.sa: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥

bg.2.61.m: Restraining them all, one should sit disciplined, intent on me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly set.
roles: Shows wisdom firm when the senses are in hand.
bg.2.61.sa: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥

bg.2.62.m: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
roles: Lets a person trace anger back to its first step.
bg.2.62.sa: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥

bg.2.63.m: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
roles: Shows knowing the sequence gives a reason to stop at the first step.
bg.2.63.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

bg.2.64.m: But a disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, attains clarity and calm.
roles: Shows serenity is the promised fruit.

bg.2.65.m: In that clarity all sorrows come to an end; for one whose mind is clear, understanding soon becomes steady.
roles: Shows serenity as the ground of both relief and steady judgement.
bg.2.65.sa: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥

bg.2.66.m: For the undisciplined there is no understanding and no steady contemplation. Without contemplation there is no peace, and for the one without peace, where is happiness?
roles: Places peace as the ground of happiness.
bg.2.66.sa: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥

bg.2.67.m: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
roles: Shows seeing which sense the mind is trailing.
bg.2.67.sa: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥

bg.2.69.m: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; and where all beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage.
roles: Names the sage awake to the self.
bg.2.69.sa: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥

bg.2.7.m: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
roles: Shows turning to someone wiser and saying teach me is the first step.
bg.2.7.sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥

bg.2.70.m: As waters enter the ocean, which is ever being filled yet stays unmoved within its shores, so the one into whom all desires enter in the same way finds peace, not the one who craves desires.
roles: Shows fullness that does not depend on what flows in.
bg.2.70.sa: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठंसमुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वेस शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥

bg.2.71.m: The person who gives up all desires and moves about free from longing, without the sense of 'mine' and without ego, attains peace.
roles: States peace is the stated fruit.
bg.2.71.sa: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥

bg.2.72.m: This is the state of Brahman, Partha. Having reached it, one is not deluded. Abiding in it even at the hour of death, one attains the peace of Brahman.
roles: Shows no delusion after reaching it.
bg.2.72.sa: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥

bg.2.8.m: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
roles: Shows even winning everything would not touch it.
bg.2.8.sa: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥

bg.3.11.m: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will attain the highest good.
roles: Shows what sustains us given back to.
bg.3.11.sa: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥

bg.3.13.m: The good who eat what remains after the offering are freed from all faults. But the wicked who cook only for themselves eat sin.
roles: Offers and shares first, then eats.
bg.3.13.sa: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥

bg.3.17.m: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
bg.3.17.sa: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥

bg.3.19.m: Therefore, always do the work that has to be done, without attachment; by working without attachment a person reaches the highest.
bg.3.19.sa: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥

bg.3.2.m: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
roles: He asks for the one thing that is surely best.
bg.3.2.sa: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥

bg.3.20.m: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. And looking to the welfare of the world, you too should act.
roles: Acts for the holding together of the world.
bg.3.20.sa: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥

bg.3.21.m: Whatever a great person does, others do the same. Whatever standard that person sets, the world follows.
roles: Shows one's conduct is what others receive and follow.
bg.3.21.sa: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥

bg.3.22.m: There is nothing in the three worlds, Partha, that I must do, nothing unattained that I need to attain, and yet I continue to act.
roles: Shows action continued purely for others.
bg.3.22.sa: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥

bg.3.25.m: As the unwise act with attachment to their work, Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing to hold the world together.
roles: Shows acting to hold the world together.

bg.3.26.m: The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Working steadily themselves, they should encourage others in all their work.
roles: Gives care not to shake someone's footing before they have another.
bg.3.26.sa: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥

bg.3.27.m: All actions are done by the qualities of nature, but the one deluded by ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'
roles: You are not the doer you take yourself to be.
bg.3.27.sa: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥

bg.3.30.m: Surrendering all actions to me, with your mind on the inner self, free from hope and the sense of 'mine', fight with your fever gone.
bg.3.30.sa: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥

bg.3.33.m: Even a wise person acts according to his own nature. Beings follow their nature; what will mere repression do?
bg.3.33.sa: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥

bg.3.34.m: Attraction and aversion to sense objects lie seated in every sense. Do not come under their power; they are your enemies on the way.
roles: Shows noticing like and dislike before they decide for you.
bg.3.34.sa: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥

bg.3.35.m: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
roles: Self-respect in doing one's own work, flaws included.
bg.3.35.sa: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥

bg.3.36.m: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?
roles: Shows asking why one does the wrong thing even when not wanting to without excuse.
bg.3.36.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥

bg.3.37.m: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.
roles: Shows knowing the enemy is the first instruction.
bg.3.37.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥

bg.3.38.m: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this wisdom covered by desire.
bg.3.38.sa: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥

bg.3.39.m: Knowledge is covered, Kaunteya, by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, an insatiable fire.
roles: Shows knowing that desire clouds even the wise.
bg.3.39.sa: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥

bg.3.4.m: Not by refraining from action does a person reach freedom from action, nor by mere renunciation does one attain perfection.
roles: Shows freedom from action as an inner state, not an absence of activity.
bg.3.4.sa: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥

bg.3.41.m: Therefore, best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, then cast off this wrongdoer that destroys knowledge and discernment.
bg.3.41.sa: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥

bg.3.42.m: The senses are said to be higher than the body; higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the self.
roles: Shows the self standing beyond senses, mind and intellect.
bg.3.42.sa: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥

bg.3.43.m: Thus knowing that which is higher than the intellect, steadying the self by the self, slay, mighty-armed one, this enemy in the form of desire, so hard to overcome.
roles: Shows that which is higher than mind and intellect within you.
bg.3.43.sa: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥

bg.3.5.m: No one can remain even for a moment without doing something; everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of nature.
roles: Shows that one will act anyway and only how.
bg.3.5.sa: न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥

bg.3.6.m: One who restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling in the mind on sense objects is deluded and is called a hypocrite.
roles: Shows holding back outwardly while feeding the craving inwardly is not restraint.
bg.3.6.sa: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥

bg.3.7.m: But one who controls the senses by the mind, Arjuna, and without attachment engages the organs of action in the yoga of action, excels.
roles: Shows senses steered by the mind.
bg.3.7.sa: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥

bg.3.8.m: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
roles: Shows settles the question of whether to act at all.
bg.3.8.sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥

bg.4.10.m: Freed from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have come to my being.
roles: Shows absorbed in him, sheltering in him.
bg.4.10.sa: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥

bg.4.11.m: In whatever way people approach me, in that same way I receive them. People follow my path in every way, Partha.
roles: Shows inviting approach in whatever form one can manage.
bg.4.11.sa: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥

bg.4.17.m: One must understand what action is, what wrong action is, and what inaction is; the way of action is deep.
bg.4.17.sa: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥

bg.4.18.m: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people; he is disciplined and does all his work.
roles: The self does nothing even while body and mind act.
bg.4.18.sa: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥

bg.4.20.m: Having given up attachment to the fruit of action, ever content and dependent on nothing, though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all.
roles: The knower acts and is not the doer.
bg.4.20.sa: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥

bg.4.21.m: Without hope, with mind and self controlled, giving up all possessiveness, doing only bodily action, he incurs no fault.
bg.4.21.sa: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥

bg.4.22.m: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
roles: Shows the same in success and failure.
bg.4.22.sa: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥

bg.4.24.m: The act of offering is Brahman, the offering is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire of Brahman. Brahman is reached by one who sees Brahman in every action.
roles: Shows every part of the act as the one reality.
bg.4.24.sa: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥

bg.4.34.m: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
roles: Shows real questioning of one who knows is named as the way to learn.
bg.4.34.sa: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥

bg.4.36.m: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
roles: Shows trust that knowledge frees from what was done.
bg.4.36.sa: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥

bg.4.37.m: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
roles: Shows knowledge of the self ends the binding of deeds.
bg.4.37.sa: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥

bg.4.38.m: There is nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds it in oneself in due time.
roles: Names knowledge as the highest purifier.
bg.4.38.sa: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥

bg.4.39.m: The person of faith, devoted to it and with senses controlled, gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, he soon reaches supreme peace.
bg.4.39.sa: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥

bg.4.40.m: The ignorant, faithless person of doubting mind perishes. For the doubting self there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
bg.4.40.sa: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥

scene.s: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.

bg.4.41.m: Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts are cut away by knowledge, and who is self-possessed, Dhananjaya.
roles: Shows self-possession not bound by what one does.
bg.4.41.sa: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥

bg.4.42.m: Therefore, cutting with the sword of knowledge this doubt in your heart born of ignorance, take refuge in yoga, and stand up, Bharata.
bg.4.42.sa: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥

bg.4.7.m: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, Bharata, then I bring myself forth.
roles: Shows trust that right is upheld.
bg.4.7.sa: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥

bg.4.8.m: To protect the good, to destroy wrongdoing, and to firmly establish dharma, I take birth age after age.
roles: Shows the good having a protector.
bg.4.8.sa: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥

bg.5.10.m: One who acts offering all actions to the Supreme, giving up attachment, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.
roles: The work is placed in God's hands.
bg.5.10.sa: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥

bg.5.11.m: With body, mind, intellect and even the senses alone, the yogis act without attachment, for the purification of the self.
roles: Names purification of the mind as the aim.
bg.5.11.sa: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥

bg.5.12.m: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
roles: Names lasting peace following giving up the fruit.
bg.5.12.sa: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥

bg.5.18.m: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and one who eats dog-meat.
roles: Shows the same Brahman in all bodies.
bg.5.18.sa: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥

bg.5.19.m: Even here the world is conquered by those whose minds are established in evenness. Brahman is flawless and the same in all; so they are established in Brahman.
roles: Evenness is resting in Brahman, which is the same in all.
bg.5.19.sa: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥

bg.5.2.m: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than renunciation of action.
roles: Shows settling the stay-or-withdraw question toward engaged action.
bg.5.2.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचसंन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥

bg.5.20.m: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
roles: Shows the evenness rests on abiding in Brahman.
bg.5.20.sa: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥

bg.5.21.m: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
roles: Names a happiness within that does not run out.
bg.5.21.sa: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥

bg.5.22.m: The enjoyments born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, Kaunteya. The wise do not delight in them.
roles: Shows not delighting in what is bound to pass.
bg.5.22.sa: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥

bg.5.23.m: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
roles: Cultivates the capacity to hold steady while the surge passes.
bg.5.23.sa: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥

bg.5.24.m: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.
bg.5.24.sa: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥

bg.5.25.m: Seers whose faults are destroyed, whose doubts are cut away, who are self-controlled and delight in the welfare of all beings, attain the peace of Brahman.
bg.5.25.sa: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥

bg.5.28.m: The sage whose senses, mind and intellect are controlled, who is intent on freedom, and from whom desire, fear and anger have gone, is truly free forever.
roles: Shows desire, fear and anger gone.
bg.5.28.sa: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥

bg.5.29.m: Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all the worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
roles: Names peace coming from knowing him so.
bg.5.29.sa: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥

bg.5.3.m: Know him to be ever a renouncer who neither hates nor desires. Free from the pairs of opposites, mighty-armed one, he is easily released from bondage.
roles: Shows the verse free of the pairs of opposites.
bg.5.3.sa: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥

bg.6.1.m: The Blessed Lord said: One who does the work that ought to be done, without depending on its fruit, is the renouncer and the yogi; not the one who gives up the sacred fire or gives up action.
roles: Staying with the work that ought to be done.
bg.6.1.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥

bg.6.16.m: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who keeps awake too long, Arjuna.
roles: Names the extremes of food and sleep as what blocks steadiness.
bg.6.16.sa: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥

bg.6.17.m: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, measured in effort at work, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
roles: A measured day makes the mind light enough for practice.
bg.6.17.sa: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥

bg.6.19.m: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker: that is the image used for the yogi of controlled mind practising union with the self.
roles: Shows the unflickering flame as a picture of stillness.
bg.6.19.sa: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥

bg.6.20.m: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, becomes still, and one sees the self by the self, one is content in the self.
roles: Shows seeing the self by the self.
bg.6.20.sa: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥

bg.6.22.m: Having gained it, one thinks no other gain greater; established in it, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.
roles: Names that as the self found in meditation.
bg.6.22.sa: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥

bg.6.23.m: Know that to be yoga: the breaking of contact with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and with an undespairing mind.
roles: Shows keeping on without losing heart.
bg.6.23.sa: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥

bg.6.25.m: Little by little one should come to rest, with understanding held steady; fixing the mind on the self, one should think of nothing else.
bg.6.25.sa: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥

bg.6.26.m: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
roles: Gives patient repetition of the same return.
bg.6.26.sa: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥

bg.6.27.m: Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is calm, whose passions are stilled, who is free from wrong and one with Brahman.
roles: Shows the highest happiness coming to the quiet mind.
bg.6.27.sa: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥

bg.6.29.m: One whose self is joined in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self; he sees the same everywhere.
roles: Shows the self in all and all in the self.
bg.6.29.sa: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥

bg.6.30.m: One who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me: I am never lost to him, and he is never lost to me.
bg.6.30.sa: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥

bg.6.32.m: One who, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.
roles: Shows others' pain is known by one's own.
bg.6.32.sa: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥

bg.6.33.m: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
bg.6.33.sa: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥

bg.6.34.m: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
roles: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn.
bg.6.34.sa: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥

bg.6.35.m: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
roles: Practice means returning again and again.
bg.6.35.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥

bg.6.36.m: Yoga is hard to reach for one whose self is uncontrolled, in my view. But one whose self is controlled and who strives can reach it by the right means.
bg.6.36.sa: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥

bg.6.37.m: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
roles: The fear of having believed, tried, slipped and not made it.
bg.6.37.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥

bg.6.38.m: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a broken cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, bewildered on the path to Brahman?
bg.6.38.sa: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥

bg.6.39.m: Krishna, please cut away this doubt of mine completely. No one but you can remove it.
roles: Shows taking doubt to the one who can answer it.
bg.6.39.sa: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥

bg.6.40.m: The Blessed Lord said: Partha, there is no ruin for him either in this world or the next. No one who does good, my friend, ever comes to grief.
roles: Shows trust that sincere effort is kept.
bg.6.40.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचपार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥

scene.s: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
scene.t: What becomes of one who falls from yoga

bg.6.43.m: There he regains the understanding of his former life, and from there strives again, more than before, for perfection, joy of the Kurus.
bg.6.43.sa: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥

bg.6.44.m: By that former practice he is carried on, even against his will. Even one who merely wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual word.
roles: Shows even the wish to know counts.
bg.6.44.sa: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥

bg.6.45.m: But the yogi who strives with diligence, cleansed of faults, perfected through many births, then reaches the highest goal.
roles: Shows perfection is gathered little by little over a long time.
bg.6.45.sa: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥

bg.6.5.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
roles: Shows the decision to be on one's own side.
bg.6.5.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

bg.6.6.m: For one who has conquered himself, the self is the friend of the self. But for one who has not, the self acts with hostility, like an enemy.
roles: Shows self-mastery turning the mind into an ally.
bg.6.6.sa: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥

bg.6.7.m: For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
roles: Shows the higher Self present to the calm, self-mastered person.
bg.6.7.sa: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥

bg.6.8.m: The yogi whose self is satisfied with knowledge and understanding, who is unshakeable, master of the senses, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are the same, is called steadfast.
roles: Names earth, stone and gold alike.
bg.6.8.sa: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥

bg.6.9.m: One who is even-minded towards well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, relatives, the good and the wicked, excels.
roles: Shows an even mind toward friend, foe, stranger, saint and wrongdoer.

bg.7.1.m: Hear, Partha, how with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking refuge in me, you will know me fully, without doubt.
bg.7.1.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥

bg.7.11.m: Of the strong, I am the strength free from desire and passion. In beings, I am desire that is not contrary to dharma, best of the Bharatas.
roles: Names strength without grasping as God's presence in the strong.
bg.7.11.sa: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥

bg.7.14.m: This divine power of mine, made of the three qualities, is very hard to get past. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.
bg.7.14.sa: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥

bg.7.16.m: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.
roles: The distressed are named first among those who come.
bg.7.16.sa: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥

bg.7.18.m: All of these are generous souls, but the wise one I regard as my very self, for with mind steadfast he has taken me as the highest goal.
roles: Takes the other as the only goal and becomes his own self.
bg.7.18.sa: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥

bg.7.21.m: Whatever form any devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that very faith of his unshakeable.
roles: Cultivates faith in whatever form is steadied.
bg.7.21.sa: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥

bg.7.27.m: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, Bharata, all beings fall into confusion at birth, scorcher of enemies.
roles: Shows seeing like and dislike as the source of confusion.
bg.7.27.sa: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥

bg.7.7.m: There is nothing higher than me, Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
bg.7.7.sa: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥

bg.8.14.m: O son of Pritha, whoever remembers me constantly, every day, with a mind turned to nothing else, for that steady seeker I am easy to reach.
bg.8.14.sa: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥

bg.8.6.m: Whatever state of being a person remembers when leaving the body at the end, to that he goes, Kaunteya, always shaped by that state.
roles: Cultivates what the mind dwells on through life as what it holds at the end.
bg.8.6.sa: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥

bg.8.7.m: Therefore remember me at all times, and fight. With mind and understanding offered to me, you will surely come to me.
roles: Mind and understanding are given to him.
bg.8.7.sa: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥

bg.8.8.m: With a mind disciplined by the practice of yoga and not straying to anything else, meditating constantly, one goes to the supreme divine Person, Partha.
roles: Shows a mind made steady by repetition.
bg.8.8.sa: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥

bg.9.17.m: I am the father of this world, the mother, the one who holds it up, the grandfather; what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.
roles: Shows turning to him as to father and mother.
bg.9.17.sa: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
